clue.text: Group of slaves given heartless greeting before endeavour

indicators.note: heartless asks for the middle letter of the greeting word to be cut out

parts.note: hello is a greeting
to endeavour is to try

explanation.surface: Captives are offered only a cold welcome before they are set to work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' takes the central L from HELLO, leaving HELO.
explanation.definitionFit: Helotry is the state or class of helots, the serfs of ancient Sparta, so a body of slaves.

clue.text: Behaviour of enamoured drunk

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters of the word before it are reeling about into a new order

explanation.surface: How someone in love behaves when they have had too much to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' looks like a description of the lover but signals the anagram of ENAMOURED.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's demeanour is their outward bearing or conduct, a close synonym.

clue.text: Pollutant from blaze enveloping yard

indicators.note: enveloping means the first piece wraps round the second

parts.note: a blaze or flash is a sudden burst of light

explanation.surface: Smoke and dirt drifting from a fire that has spread across a yard.
explanation.definitionFit: Fly ash is the fine residue carried up the chimney from burning coal, an air pollutant.

clue.text: Withdrawal of support given to Bangor locality

parts.note: to back is to support
Bangor in Northern Ireland lies in County Down

explanation.surface: A political party pulls its support from a town in Wales or Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: Bangor here is the Northern Irish town in County Down, a county of Northern Ireland, not the Welsh city.
explanation.definitionFit: A backdown is a retreat from a position or claim, so a withdrawal.

clue.text: When in trouble, first subtly seek gestures of affection

indicators.note: in trouble suggests the following words are in disorder and need rearranging

explanation.surface: When a relationship is struggling, one should start by quietly looking for loving signs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in trouble' rearranges all fifteen letters of FIRST SUBTLY SEEK.
explanation.definitionFit: Butterfly kisses are made by fluttering one's eyelashes against another's skin, a tender caress.

clue.text: Happy families maybe worry about daughter going to school

indicators.note: about means the first word goes around the pieces that follow

parts.note: care is worry or anxiety
a gam is a school of whales

explanation.surface: Content households perhaps fret over a daughter starting school.
explanation.walkthrough: Happy Families is a children's card game of collecting family sets; GAM, a school of whales, is a rare word.
explanation.definitionFit: Happy Families is one example of a game played with cards, hence 'maybe'.

clue.text: Expression of annoyance with France's leader spiking plan

indicators.note: spiking means one piece is driven into the middle of the other

parts.note: drat is a mild curse

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A grumbling remark as the French president upsets a proposed scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: A draft is a preliminary version or outline, a plan to be worked up.

clue.text: Vacillate when having to entertain two females

indicators.note: having to entertain means the first word holds the next piece inside it as a host holds guests

parts.note: while can mean when, as in 'while I was out'
F is the abbreviation for female, twice

explanation.surface: Someone dithers when they are obliged to host a couple of women.
explanation.definitionFit: To whiffle is to waver or shift about, as a wind or an undecided person does.

clue.text: First person brought in to promote female author

indicators.note: brought in to means the first piece is put inside the next

parts.note: to sell a product is to promote it
we is the first person plural pronoun

explanation.surface: A publisher hires a leading figure to push a woman writer's book.
explanation.definitionFit: Anna Sewell was the English novelist who wrote Black Beauty.

clue.text: Water creature beginning to plod, getting stuck in ground

indicators.note: getting stuck in means one piece is lodged inside the other

parts.note: terrain is ground or land

indicators.note: beginning to asks for just the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A slow-moving animal begins to trudge and finds itself bogged down in mud.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrapin is a small freshwater turtle, an aquatic reptile.

clue.text: Front of stronghold occupied by soldiers each year

indicators.note: occupied by means the first piece holds the following pieces inside it

parts.note: a fort is a stronghold
RE, the Royal Engineers, are soldiers
PA is per annum, Latin for each year

explanation.surface: The front of a fortress is held by troops every year.
explanation.definitionFit: The forepart of something is its foremost section, its front.

clue.text: At end of journey posh fellow escaped

indicators.note: At end of places the posh fellow after the journey word

parts.note: to go is to journey
a toff is a posh, upper-class man

explanation.surface: An upper-class man slips away once his trip is over.
explanation.definitionFit: To get off is to escape, especially to avoid punishment or harm.

clue.text: Old platter of fish King's tucked into — and Queen

indicators.note: tucked into means the King letter is slipped inside the fish

parts.note: a tench is a freshwater fish
R is Rex, king; the 's stands for 'is'
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: An antique dish holding fish that the King and Queen have eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: A trencher was a wooden board or plate on which food was served in earlier times.

clue.text: Made fish crumble, being very hungry

indicators.note: crumble suggests the letters break up and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cook makes a fish crumble because the family is starving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crumble' reads as the dish but signals rearranging MADE FISH.
explanation.definitionFit: Famished is an intensified synonym for hungry, starving.

clue.text: Pose with mouth snarled in violent movie

indicators.note: snarled means tangled, so the letters are knotted into a new order

explanation.surface: An actor strikes a pose and bares his teeth in an action film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snarled' suggests a sneer but means tangled, rearranging POSE and MOUTH.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoot-'em-up is a film or game full of gunfights and violent action.

clue.text: Like some wood or like some rock found at bottom of lake

indicators.note: found at bottom of places the rock word beneath the lake letter in this down entry

parts.note: igneous rock is formed from molten magma

explanation.surface: Is it wood or stone lying on the floor of a lake?
explanation.definitionFit: Ligneous means woody, made of or resembling wood, from Latin lignum.

clue.text: Poverty as blemish on Cambridge?

parts.note: a scar is a blemish on the skin
Cambridge is an example of a city, signalled by the question mark

explanation.surface: Is deprivation a stain on a famous university town?
explanation.definitionFit: Scarcity and poverty both mean a shortage or lack of something.

clue.text: Grumble about horse chasing fox

parts.note: C is circa, about
a hunter is a horse ridden in fox hunting

explanation.surface: Someone complains about a horse in pursuit of a fox.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like a link to the horse but gives C, from circa.
explanation.definitionFit: To chunter is to mutter or grumble, a British colloquial verb.

clue.text: Put in a new chair perhaps in auditorium or reception

indicators.note: in auditorium means as heard by an audience in a hall

parts.words: Put in a new chair perhaps
parts.note: to reseat someone is to put them in a different chair

explanation.surface: Moving a guest to another chair in a theatre or at a welcome party.
explanation.definitionFit: Receipt is the act of receiving something, a formal synonym for reception.

clue.text: Swoon and weep endlessly when meeting sweetheart

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter of the weeping word is dropped

parts.note: to keen is to wail or weep in grief
a lover is a sweetheart

explanation.surface: Fainting and crying without stop on seeing one's beloved again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts the N from KEEN, leaving KEE.
explanation.definitionFit: To keel over is to collapse or faint, which is what a swoon is.

clue.text: Bishop of Exeter not half cunning

indicators.note: not half means only half of the Exeter word is kept

parts.note: Exon., from Latin Exoniensis, is the signature of the Bishop of Exeter
arch can mean sly or cunning

explanation.surface: A churchman of Exeter is only half as crafty as he seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half' keeps EX of EXON, the Latin abbreviation the Bishop of Exeter signs by.
explanation.definitionFit: An exarch is a senior bishop in the Eastern Orthodox churches, ranking above a metropolitan.

clue.text: In Paris we turned back with two thousand in rally

indicators.note: in means the thousands are placed inside the reversed word
turned back means the French word is read from right to left

parts.note: nous is French for we
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, twice

explanation.surface: French protesters retreat, then two thousand of them gather again.
explanation.definitionFit: To summon or rally is to call together or muster, as one summons courage.

clue.text: Two mothers and demanding girl?

parts.note: Two mothers asks for two different mother words; the first is ma, an informal mother
the second mother is dam, the mother of an animal

explanation.surface: A household with two mums and a bossy daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: A madam is a precocious, imperious little girl who expects her own way.

clue.text: Long-distance travellers in camp seen misbehaving

indicators.note: misbehaving suggests the letters are unruly and out of place

explanation.surface: Wayfarers spotted in a campsite are causing trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Spacemen are astronauts, who journey vast distances beyond Earth.

clue.text: Academic boss, 26

parts.note: a stud is a boss, a raised ornamental knob
the answer to 26 Across means guarantees, and IOUs are promises to pay

explanation.surface: A head of department described by a cross-reference.
explanation.walkthrough: '26' points to the answer to 26 Across, PROMISES, whose synonym IOUS is needed here.
explanation.definitionFit: Studious and academic both describe someone devoted to study and learning.

clue.text: What's evident in fifty bactrian camels and asses

parts.note: Bactrian camels have two humps each, so fifty have a hundred, C in Roman numerals
humps are what one sees on camels

explanation.surface: A puzzling question about what can be seen on a herd of two-humped camels.
explanation.walkthrough: Fifty Bactrians times two humps makes a hundred, C, then HUMPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Chumps are fools, the same as asses in the figurative sense.

clue.text: Guarantees for young lady with inner energy

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

indicators.note: with inner means the energy letter sits inside the young lady word

parts.note: a miss is a young lady
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Assurances given in favour of a girl with lots of spark inside her.
explanation.definitionFit: Promises are pledges or assurances, the same as guarantees in the plural noun sense.
